slides.heading: Conditionals with User Input
slides.body: Conditionals with User Input is part of Conditional Execution. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Conditionals with User Input
slides.body: Conditionals can use user input after converting it to the needed type. This lets the program decide based on values entered by the learner.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: A conditional with input is like a guard asking your age before deciding which entrance you can use.

annotations.note: This line stores or updates a value using a variable.
This line checks a condition before running the indented code.
This line displays a value or message on the screen.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: A conditional needs a colon, correct indentation, and a condition that clearly evaluates to True or False.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Ask for an age, convert it to int, and print Adult if it is at least 18.

quiz.prompt_text: Why do you need int() when using input() with a number comparison?

options: Because input() only works with booleans
Because input() returns text and you cannot compare text to a number directly
Because int() is required before every print()
Because Python cannot read numbers from the keyboard

quiz.explanation: Exactly! input() always returns a string. To compare it as a number (like score >= 75), you must first convert it using int() or float().

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines to read a score from the user and print 'Passed' if it is at least 75.
quiz.explanation: The input is collected and converted to int first, then the if statement checks the value, and the indented print runs only when the condition is True.

quiz.prompt_text: Ask the user for an age, convert it to an integer, and print 'Adult' if it is at least 18.

content.hint: Use if age >= 18: then indent print("Adult") below it.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: int(input("Age: ")) converts the user input to an integer. Then if age >= 18: with indented print("Adult") makes the decision based on the entered value.
